item.title: Cyber resilience: building confidence as threats evolve
item.description: Speech by Mark Francis, director of specialists at the Cyber Security in Financial Services Summit. There is no shortage of material for a speech about cyber security at the moment. Last month was the highest month for cyber incidents reported to the FCA in the past 18 months, and the second highest in the past 5 years.

item.title: Progressive targets $100m one-year aggregate Bonanza Re 2026-1 catastrophe bond
item.description: Progressive, the US insurance company, has returned to the catastrophe bond market aiming to secure $100 million or more of annual aggregate, multi-peril reinsurance protection from the capital markets, through a Bonanza Re Ltd. Like last year, Progressive is aiming to secure additional aggregate property catastrophe reinsurance in fully-collateralized form through this catastrophe bond, with but this time spread across two tranches of discounted notes that are being offered. A year ago, Progressive secured $125 million of aggregate catastrophe reinsurance limit from the also one-year duration Bonanza Re Ltd.

item.title: Boards approve SCOR and Japan Post Insurance’s reinsurance vehicle partnership
item.description: Global reinsurance firm SCOR and Japan Post Insurance are moving forward with a longevity reinsurance transaction valued at roughly ¥3 trillion in policy reserves, anchored by a new SCOR-managed Bermuda reinsurance vehicle in which Japan Post Insurance will invest approximately ¥81 billion into. With both companies having received approval from their respective boards to implement the deal, which was first announced in a July 2026 memorandum of understanding, Japan Post Insurance will cede longevity risk from a portion of its pre-privatisation contracts, in-payout whole-life annuity policies to SCOR. SCOR and Japan Post Insurance also confirmed that the ¥3 trillion figure is based on current estimates and is subject to change depending on the reinsurance contracts and trends in the market environment used as the basis for valuation.

item.title: Cat bonds hold rate advantage, as principal loss remains primary risk for investors: King Ridge
item.description: A recent report from King Ridge Capital Advisors LLC, the specialist insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager, has highlighted how catastrophe bonds differ from traditional fixed-rate bonds in their interest rate sensitivity, while emphasising that the primary risk for investors remains loss of principal rather than rising yields. The spread is set when the bond is priced and reflects the modeled chance of loss and market conditions at the time,” King Ridge explains. Catastrophe bonds have a different interest-rate structure.

item.title: Lloyd’s targets more joined-up oversight as 2027 business plan points to disciplined growth
item.description: Alongside the oversight priorities, Rachel Turk, Lloyd’s Chief of Performance & Strategy, set out the headline figures underpinning Lloyd’s 2027 business plan, which points to a focus on profitable growth and underwriting discipline. Lloyd’s is planning a more joined-up approach to market oversight in 2027, bringing together supervisory focus on underwriting risk, solvency, and conduct and governance, as the market looks to improve consistency and direct attention towards the risks that matter most. The figures reportedly reflect Lloyd’s aim of balancing growth with profitability, with the business plan framed around disciplined expansion rather than volume alone.

item.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire technology consulting firm Synpulse
item.description: Oliver Wyman, a global management consulting firm and a Marsh business, has entered into an agreement to acquire Synpulse, a global technology consulting and AI platform company. Ted Moynihan, President and CEO of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting, said, “Our clients don’t separate strategy from technology and execution—they need great ideas to deliver real change. Oliver Wyman and Synpulse have already been working together, with combined teams delivering multiple end-to-end transformations for clients.

item.title: Testudo provides AI agent insurance to AI-native law firm Crosby
item.description: Testudo, the specialist artificial intelligence (AI) liability insurer and Lloyd’s coverholder, has insured the agents of Crosby, a New York-based AI-native law firm. Testudo, considered the biggest specialist insurer of standalone AI liability insurance for US companies, according to the firm, has issued policy protection for Crosby backed by Lloyd’s of London. “AI native companies like Crosby represent exactly the kind of business we built Testudo to support,” said Testudo CEO and Co-founder George Lewin-Smith.

item.title: VIG nine-month profit tops €1bn
item.description: Vienna Insurance Group (VIG) lifted profit before taxes by 15.4% to €1,007.3m in the first nine months of 2026, its first nine-month result above €1bn. Profit before taxes of more than EUR 1 billion after nine months also reflects our raised outlook for the full year 2026." In October, VIG raised its full-year 2026 profit before taxes outlook to €1.35bn to €1.4bn. Growth in profit was driven mainly by the Extended CEE segment, with significant contributions from Bulgaria, Romania, Slovakia, and Hungary.

item.title: AXA UK & Ireland names Jon Walker interim CEO
item.description: AXA has appointed Jon Walker, CEO of AXA Insurance UK, as Interim CEO of AXA UK & Ireland as Tara Foley departs to pursue opportunities outside the group, Reinsurance News reported. Jon Walker said: "I’m proud to take up the position of Interim CEO for AXA UK & AXA Ireland. Walker is a board member of AXA Insurance UK plc and a non-executive on the AXA Ireland DAC board.

item.title: Arch MI secures $202.5m reinsurance through Bellemeade Re
item.description: Arch Mortgage Insurance Company (Arch MI) has obtained $202.5m of indemnity reinsurance on a pool of about $55bn of mortgages from Bellemeade Re 2026-1 Ltd., a special purpose reinsurer. Since the Bellemeade programme began in 2015, Arch has completed 23 transactions securing nearly $10bn of indemnity reinsurance. Bellemeade Re 2026-1 funds its obligations through five classes of amortising notes with 10-year legal final maturities.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Investments backs Synergy Pet Group
item.description: Liberty Mutual Investments announced on November 10 that it provided debt financing to Synergy Pet Group, a Lakewood, New Jersey-based provider of pet benefits and veterinary software. Liberty Mutual Investments previously backed Synergy in 2023 alongside LoneTree Capital. Synergy offers pet insurance, wellness plans, and veterinary discounts through Wishbone, formerly known as Pet Benefit Solutions.

item.title: L&G expands mortgage distribution network
item.description: Legal & General (L&G) has added Monmouthshire Building Society to its Mortgage Club lender panel and mortgage sourcing platform, Ignite. The partnership gives mortgage brokers access to a wider range of lending products, including residential mortgages, self-employed lending, buy-to-let, holiday let, and portfolio lending. Through Ignite, brokers can compare Monmouthshire’s mortgage products, review eligibility criteria, and generate European Standardised Information Sheets (ESIS) within a single platform.

item.title: Comunicado: Akurateco fortalece su presencia en Latinoamérica con la ampliación de su equipo local
item.description: Contenido de la comunidad: Akurateco, proveedor internacional de tecnología de orquestación de pagos y pasarelas de pago de marca blanca, anuncia el fortalecimiento de su presencia en América Latina (LATAM) mediante la incorporación de profesionales locales a sus operaciones regionales. La expansión se apoya en las actividades que Akurateco ya desarrolla en Latinoamérica, incluidas sus integraciones tecnológicas y alianzas estratégicas con actores del ecosistema de pagos. Con una mayor presencia local, la compañía busca reforzar las relaciones comerciales, impulsar nuevas oportunidades de colaboración y responder a las necesidades específicas de los mercados latinoamericanos.

item.title: Authorities complete 2026 review of payments Memorandum of Understanding
item.description: The Bank of England (the Bank), Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) have completed their annual review of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on payments. The review found that cooperation and coordination remain effective, with respondents welcoming tangible progress in how the Authorities work together. Following the review, the Authorities have concluded that no changes to the MoU are needed at this time.

item.title: Investors maintaining ILS allocations shows where they see relative value: Sapelza, Lumen Re
item.description: As institutional investors constantly compare catastrophe risk with private credit, infrastructure, emerging market debt, as well as other alternatives, the fact that many continue to consistently maintain their insurance-linked securities (ILS) allocations heavily shows where they see value today, Klaus Sapelza, Chief Underwriting Officer at Lumen Re told Artemis. The fact that many continue to maintain their ILS allocations indicates where they see value today.” Moreover, the overall market consensus is that reinsurance pricing will further soften by 2027, which according to Sapelza, should not concern ILS investors. Most of the investors we speak with focus on relative value.

item.title: PERILS finalises industry loss estimate for Queensland & New South Wales SCS at AU $3.1bn
item.description: Catastrophe data aggregator PERILS has published its fourth and final industry loss estimate for the severe convective storms that impacted Queensland and New South Wales between November 21st to 27th, 2025, placing the insurance market loss at AU $3.132 billion, a 6% increase from the firm’s third loss estimate. The event primarily affected the states of Queensland, which contributed 93% of the total industry loss, while New South Wales accounted 7% of the loss total. We covered PERILS’ initial industry loss estimate for these severe convective storms back in January, where losses at the time had reached AU $2.663 billion.

item.title: Alignment and transparency key to sustainable casualty sidecar capacity: Artex CEO Faries
item.description: As momentum continues to build within the casualty sidecar market, Kathleen Faries of Artex Capital Solutions has outlined that pairing strong underwriting fundamentals with greater structural transparency and sponsor-investor alignment could create a sustainable force of casualty capacity and a more durable relationship between the insurance and asset-management markets. Earlier this year, rating agency S&P Global highlighted a structural shift in the sidecar market, with casualty reinsurance sidecars growing to account for approximately 10% of total sidecar capacity. Faries made these comments in Artex Capital Solutions’ latest Alternative View report.

item.title: California Department of Insurance completes sustainable insurance roadmap and introduces new insurability framework
item.description: The California Department of Insurance (CDI), the government agency responsible for regulating insurers and overseeing consumer protection in California’s insurance market, has completed its four-year Sustainable Insurance Roadmap and introduced a new framework designed to address the challenges of maintaining insurance coverage in areas exposed to increasing climate-related risks. The announcement was accompanied by the publication of Preserving Insurability, a report examining the outcomes of the initiative and setting out the principles behind the newly established California Framework for Insurable Communities. According to CDI, the Sustainable Insurance Roadmap was introduced in 2022 as the first programme of its kind internationally, seeking to examine how insurance regulation could respond to environmental threats while supporting market stability and policyholder protection.

item.title: AXIS appoints Trevor Pinos as Senior Underwriter, North America Casualty Reinsurance
item.description: AXIS, a global specialty insurer and reinsurer, has announced the appointment of Trevor Pinos as Senior Underwriter, North America Casualty Reinsurance. In his new role, Pinos will support AXIS’ casualty reinsurance portfolio across North America, with a focus on General Liability and Workers Compensation. Pinos joins AXIS from AM Specialty Insurance Group, where he served as Vice President, Reinsurance/Program Underwriting.

item.title: Optalitix launches agentic AI within quote platform to automate underwriting workflows
item.description: Optalitix, the pricing and underwriting insurtech, has introduced agentic AI capabilities into its Optalitix Quote platform, allowing insurers, reinsurers and managing general agents (MGAs) to automate complex underwriting activities while retaining control over decisions. The productivity improvements demonstrated by the new agentic AI technology include quote processing and quote reviews that have dropped from hour to seconds. “Our agentic AI cuts tasks that previously took hours or weeks to seconds or minutes, while working within insurers’ existing pricing models and approval processes.

item.title: Recoop Disaster raises $6 million
item.description: Strategic Product Partners, the West Des Moines, Iowa-based company behind Recoop Disaster Insurance , reported selling $5.96 million in debt securities to 16 investors as part of a $10.42 million offering, according to a Form D filed November 23. Recoop offers supplemental disaster insurance to homeowners and renters, with lump-sum cash benefits ranging from $5,000 to $25,000 after a qualifying event. The first sale took place on November 13, and $4.46 million remained available at the time of filing.

item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Crosby’s deployment is notable because the firm presents its AI agents as part of the delivery of legal services rather than simply as internal productivity tools. “Our goal is to be ahead of the curve as AI agents become capable of doing more legal work,” comments Ryan Daniels, CEO, Crosby.

item.title: Nvidia, Board Still Face Legal Risks After Huang’s Return
item.description: Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO at the urging of US President Donald Trump, less than two weeks after the co-founder of the AI chip powerhouse resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China. Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia to make repeated assurances about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, until the allegations were public.

item.title: Coastal Storms Could Put a Damper on Thanksgiving Plans
item.description: Storms across the Southeast and along the West Coast will bring scattered showers and thunderstorms, while chillier air around the Mississippi Valley could also bring snow and rain just in time to snarl Wednesday travel plans, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). A West Coast storm brings along the chance of more high tides which could lead to coastal flooding. A strong Thanksgiving Day storm threatens the Ohio Valley to the Eastern Seaboard, bringing with it windy conditions, heavy rain, and flooding risk.

item.title: How should investors evaluate performance?
item.description: Before selling a fund that has underperformed its benchmark, investors should ask why and whether it still meets their needs. So, the first question isn’t simply: ‘Did this fund beat the market?’ Instead, investors should ask: ‘Is this fund fulfilling its intended role?’ That means looking at its stated objective, strategy and style (for example, whether it invests in particular countries or sectors, or favours value or growth companies). Investors should also consider the portfolio’s overall balance of risk and return and the timeframe for assessing results.

item.title: Reinsurance renewals running later than usual, focus remains largely on price: Althoff, Hannover Re
item.description: Sven Althoff, Member of the Executive Board for Property & Casualty at Hannover Re, explained this morning that the reinsurance renewals are running later than usual in many areas and while rate adequacy is expected for many parts of the portfolio, he acknowledged there may be a need to start cycle managing due to price pressures. Speaking during the Hannover Re investor day held in London today, Althoff said that with the January 2027 renewals running behind their typical end of year schedule, it means data points are still lacking as to how much rates may move at 1/1. Althoff explained that as the January 2027 reinsurance renewals approach, pressure on the pricing environment continues to be seen, echoing what was discussed with Hannover Re’s clients at the Monte Carlo event in September.

item.title: Hannover Re Capital Partners seeing “quite huge interest” from investors: Sehm
item.description: “But, especially with HCP, Hannover Re Capital Partners, quite huge interest from investors to connect our nat cat business with third-party capital, so we are on a good journey on that.” Sehm later explained that Hannover Re’s corporate strategy shows priorities are accessing risk, evaluating risk and transforming risk, with the ILS business highly relevant strategically. Speaking at Hannover Re’s investor day in London today, board member Silke Sehm explained that investor interest in ILS management unit Hannover Re Capital Partners is significant, while fellow-board member Sven Althoff explained why the reinsurer has so far not ventured into casualty ILS or other lines of business. Hannover Re Executive Board Member Silke Sehm noted that all insurance-linked securities activities continue to increase across the company’s different areas of focus, from facilitation and service provision, through to the more recent addition of ILS investment management under the Bermuda-based Hannover Re Capital Partners unit.

item.title: Oliver Wyman names Netherton as Global Head & Moloney as Executive Chair, Insurance & Asset Management
item.description: Oliver Wyman, a global management consulting firm and a Marsh business, has promoted George Netherton as Global Head of Insurance and Asset Management (IAM), effective immediately. He succeeds Michael Moloney, who will transition to Executive Chair of Insurance and Asset Management while maintaining leadership roles in risk and insurance consulting at Oliver Wyman Actuarial and Marsh Risk. The firm explained that Moloney led the business through a period of significant growth and expansion and will continue to work closely with Netherton on its strategic development, while strengthening collaboration across Oliver Wyman and Marsh.

item.title: Cedar Trace receives Lloyd’s Permission to Underwrite for Syndicate 1503
item.description: The syndicate will write diversified reinsurance business alongside a delegated direct insurance portfolio, marking a significant expansion of Cedar Trace’s existing Bermuda-based reinsurance and asset management platform into the Lloyd’s market.” David Croom-Johnson, Executive Chairman, added, “We are building out a very strong team to establish Syndicate 1503, and throughout 2027 we will seek to bring in further talent to support our longer-term goals of growth across all three Cedar Trace platforms – Syndicate 1503, Mereo Insurance Limited and Cedar Trace Capital Management.” Lorraine Harfitt, CEO of Asta, said, “We are delighted to have partnered with Cedar Trace to establish its Lloyd’s platform and secure permission to underwrite. Cedar Trace Underwriting has received Permission to Underwrite from Lloyd’s to write business for the 2027 Year of Account. Through Syndicate 1503, Cedar Trace will gain an additional source of underwriting capacity and access to Lloyd’s distribution network, complementing and adding scale to its existing Bermuda platform.

item.title: Price Forbes launches dedicated Healthcare & Life Sciences division, appoints Henry as CEO
item.description: Specialist insurance broking firm Price Forbes has announced the launch of Healthcare & Life Sciences as a standalone specialist division, with Dominic Henry as CEO. Formerly part of the Casualty division, this new structure consolidates Price Forbes’ healthcare and life sciences expertise into dedicated business pillar, focused exclusively on serving healthcare providers, life sciences companies and related organisations worldwide. We have an exceptional group of specialists across healthcare and life sciences, led by Daniel, Neil and Tomer, and this structure will allow us to deepen collaboration, enhance our client proposition and continue investing in the talent and capabilities required to support future growth.” John Thompson, CEO of Price Forbes, said: “The establishment of Healthcare & Life Sciences as a standalone division marks an important milestone in the evolution of Price Forbes.

item.title: How Will This Year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Weather the Storm?
item.description: The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is set for Thursday morning in New York City, but gusty winds and periods of heavy rain in the forecast could keep its famous giant character balloons close to the ground. Under New York City safety rules, 34 mph is the maximum wind gust limit — alongside a 23 mph sustained wind cap — for flying giant balloons at the Thanksgiving Day Parade. Related : How Niche Insurance Shielded Bad Bunny From Bad Weather Those limits were established after the 1997 parade, when gusts over 40 mph slammed The Cat in the Hat balloon into a lamppost on Central Park West.

item.title: Australian Regulator Finds More Suspected Audit Misconduct at Big Four Firms
item.description: Australia’s corporate regulator said on Wednesday it has discovered dozens of additional cases of suspected audit misconduct among the Big Four accounting firms, ranging from misuse of client information to falsified work. The Australian government is considering breaking up the Big Four firms and imposing partnership size caps as well as stipulating a mandatory rotation of audit firms in a bid to clean up the sector. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said it was now considering its enforcement and regulatory options following its review of 558 audit complaints at KPMG, PwC, Deloitte and EY.

item.title: Army Detonates Hazardous Material in Iowa Despite Outcry
item.description: The Army blew up five tons of hazardous materials stored at a facility in Iowa, proceeding with the move despite concerns from US lawmakers and environmental groups that the open-air detonation risked sending a plume of lead dust over surrounding communities a day before Thanksgiving. On X, the Army had said it would proceed with a “controlled, mitigated detonation” at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Despite concerns about contamination, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals had concluded Monday that the US Environmental Protection Agency had “adequately incorporated safeguards to minimize the dispersal of lead dust into the environment.” “We are committed to the safety and health of the people of this region, and we will do everything in our power to protect them,” Adam Telle, the acting Army secretary, said in a statement on X on Tuesday night.
